Appearance:
 Shri Kapil Pathak - Advocate for the applicant.
Shri Akhilendra Singh - Govt. Advocate for respondent/ Sta

ORDER This is the second application filed by the applicant under Section 482 of BNSS, 2023 (Section 438 of CrPC, 1973) for grant of anticipatory bail relating to FIR No.27/2023 dated 14.1.2023, registered at Police Station - Satna Kotwali, District Satna (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under Sections 498A, 377/34 of IPC and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
Applicant apprehending her arrest in the aforesaid offence has again knocked at the portal of this Court for grant of anticipatory bail.

2. Applicant's first bail application was dismissed as withdrawn and not pressed vide order dated 19.4.2023 passed in M.Cr.C. No.16269/2023 with liberty to file the same whenever applicant reaches to India.
3. As per the prosecution story, complainant/wife marriage was solemnized with the co-accused Shantanu Nandan on 11.07.2019.
They remained together almost for a period of more than two years.

On 14.01.2023 prosecutrix submitted an application in writing before police City Kotwali,
Satna alleging that just after marriage, co-accused Shantanu Nandan along with applicant tortured and harassed NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:16397 2 MCRC-7171-2025 her in connection with demand of dowry i.e. one gold chain, one Innova vehicle or Rs. 15,00,000/- (Fifty Lakh) cash.
In marriage, her parents had spent almost Rs.18,00,000/-.

It is further alleged that Smt. Hema Shrivastava vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196619743/

sentences.text: during matrimonial life, she had conceived but co-accused Shantanu Nandan was not willing to have a child.
Therefore, he himself and at the behest of applicant, gave her some medicine for miscarriage and due to effect of that medicine her fetus got aborted.
It is further alleged that on 24.01.2022 co-accused Shantanu Nandan along with the complainant came to Satna and stayed with her in Bharhut Hotel.
In hotel without her consent he committed unnatural sex with her causing lot of pain.
On 26.01.2022, he left the hotel without giving any information to her and others.
It is further alleged that at various occasions co-accused Shantanu Nandan committed carnal intercourse with her against in ordinary course of nature.
On the basis of written complaint, FIR was registered and applicant has been arrested.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant has returned to India on 8.2.2025 and at present she is residing at Bangalore.
It is contended that applicant is innocent.
She has not committed any offence.
She has been falsely implicated only because she is the sister of the husband of complainant.

Applicant is residing with her husband and family either at Bangalore or at Paris,
where her husband is working at Working Visa.
She has nothing to do with commission of offence.
She never lived with the complainant and her husband either at Satna or in some part of India.
She has been enroped in offence just to pressurize the co-accused Shantanu Nandan to withdraw his divorce petition pending before the competent Court.
She is permanent resident of Bangalore but she often visits Paris where her husband is working.
She shall abide by all the conditions whatsoever imposed by this Court.

Therefore, it is prayed that applicant may be released on anticipatory bail.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:16397 3 MCRC-7171-2025 5.
On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant and disputes her presence in India.
It is submitted that no concrete proof has been filed before the Court to show that at present, she is residing at Bangalore.
6. Admittedly, the present applicant is the married sister of complainant's husband.
The only allegation against her is that she had harassed the complainant in connection with demand of dowry and had got fetus aborted as husband of complainant was not willing to have a child.
It is undisputed that matrimonial disputes are pending between the complainant and her husband.
FIR has been lodged almost after one year of the last incident as alleged in the complaint in writing.
Applicant is a married lady and she is living with her husband at Bangalore and Paris (France).
It is a case in which custodial interrogation of applicant/accused is not required.
Therefore, without expressing any opinion on the merit of the case, I am of the view that it is a case in which applicant Hema Shrivastava may be released on bail.

Consequently, second anticipatory bail application under Section 482 of BNSS, 2023/ Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant - Smt. Hema Shrivastava stands allowed subject to the condition that applicant shall remain present in person before the Investigation Officer at the time of furnishing bail.

7 . It is directed that in the event of arrest applicant- Smt. Hema Shrivastava be released on bail on her furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs. 50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Authority.

At stage of filing of charge-sheet by police, applicant shall furnish fresh bail bond of same amount before trial Court to its satisfaction subject to following conditions:-

(i) Applicant shall make herself available for interrogation by a police NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:16397 4 MCRC-7171-2025 officer as and when required;
(ii) Applicant is directed to join investigation, then and there.

(iii) Applicant shall not, directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade them from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer;

(iv) In case, applicant is not arrested within a period of 08 days by the Investigation Officer, she shall surrender herself before the Investigation Officer within 10 days' from today failing which this order shall become ineffective.

8. However, it is being made clear that in case of bail jump and in violation of any of conditions imposed herein above, this order shall become ineffective and Investigation Officer/Trial Court shall be at liberty to proceed against the applicant as per law.
